newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Germany bids for S.African naval contract.
newsitem.headline: Germany bids for S.African naval contract.

text.p: German industrialists met South African Defence Minister Joe Modise on Friday to promote a 10 billion rand proposal to build ships and planes for President Nelson Mandela's post-apartheid defence force, officials said.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) South African representative Wilhelm Lehmann told Reuters he was meeting Modise in Pretoria but declined to give further details.
This was confirmed by a German diplomat, who said a consortium of German industries had made a proposal which included significant technology transfer guarantees.

Tony Yengeni, chairman of parliament's influential Standing Committee on Defence, said bidding for a South African armaments contract would be reopened as soon as parliament has approved a Defence Review adopted by the cabinet in June.
Parliament is due to vote on the proposal later this month.
The navy has only nine small surface strike craft and three aged French submarines to patrol its 2,000 mile coastline.

Mandela shelved a long-running tender programme for four naval corvettes, equivalent to European light frigates, last year, saying the nation was not adequately united on the need to re-equip its run down navy.
The process was halted after the search had been narrowed from 42 original bids to rival 1.7 billion rand ($362 million) offers by Britain's Yarrow shipyard and Spain's Bazan ship builders.

Britain has subsequently offered South Africa four unused Upholder class submarines at a knockdown price of two billion rand and has put forward a package including the submarines and four purpose-built corvettes.
France, knocked out in the original tender process, also has made a new proposal for ships and submarines.
"What is absolutely certain is that we will not just go back to the British and Spanish bids," Yengeni said.
"We have to take another look at the process and decide how to include the new British bid as well as offers from France and Germany," he said.

The German diplomat, who asked not to be identified, said Daimler Benz and the Blohm and Voss shipyard of Hamburg -- a unit of Thyssen Industrie AG -- had put together a package to build corvettes, helicopters and jets.
The package includes a proposed joint venture by South Africa's Denel Aviation, Daimler Benz and Hyundai of Korea to develop an advanced jet trainer with possible assembly in South Africa.
The diplomat confirmed details published by the Johannesburg-based Business Day in a report from Bonn, which estimated the value of the deal at around 10 billion dollars.
